item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Bexided,

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: SCP-XXXX - 4D Pocket
item.content:encoded:
Item #: XXXX

Object Class: Safe
Secondary Class: Taumiel
Disruption Class: Vlam
Risk Class: Notice

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX is to be kept in High-Value Storage Locker 53D at Site-19 when not being utilized for testing and/or research purposes. The item is safe to handle, and poses no known threats of any kind, though due to its nature, it could be highly powerful depending on the utilization. No human subjects or other SCP's are to be produced out of SCP-XXXX at any time. No personnel with the exception of Class-D personnel with low IQ scores are allowed to enter SCP-XXXX under any circumstance. SCP-XXXX can only be accessed by personnel with level 2 clearance or above, and may occasionally be utilized as a form of additional resources when lack thereof.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a white semi-circle pocket composed of standard rubber. SCP-XXXX is capable of producing any kind of physical object or person a subject desires so long as the said object or person exists and the subject reaches into SCP-XXXX. In order to achieve this, it has been determined that SCP-XXXX can connect with the minds of those who reach in. The size of the objects produced are irrelevant as SCP-XXXX is capable of expanding in size to the exact measurements of the object produced. Objects can also be inserted into SCP-XXXX with minimal struggle.

The quantity of the objects is also irrelevant, as the objects produced are an exact clone of the original copy. Should the original object be specified, it will be produced, though said object will now reside in the location of the production in lieu of its original one. Both SCP-XXXX and the items within remain unaffected by liquids poured inside, though they can be affected upon full production.

SCP-XXXX’s externally measures 8.5 inches in diameter, 4.25 inches in radius, 2 millimeters in thickness, 14 grams in weight, and should two meet, it would have a circumference of approximately 27 inches. SCP-XXXX’s internal measurements are immeasurable. After several tests, it has been determined that SCP-XXXX is 4-Dimensional, causing its internal dimensions and mass to be practically incomprehensible, hence the nickname “4D Pocket”.

SCP-XXXX is also capable of sticking to any solid surface after applying pressure, and can be removed from said surface with ease. To date, SCP-XXXX has shown no other anomalous properties.

item.title: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not until critiqued.

Page Type: SCP Article / Tale.

Genre (Optional): Drama (Possibly something else, but I can't think of what it'd be.)

Page Layout (Optional): It'd begin as a tale. After a medium amount of writing in the tale, it'd then show an entry of the SCP - at least, what is understood about them at that point. Then switching back to tale, then after more is learnt, the document is updated again. Repeat this until the document is fully written, ending with a short note.

Elevator Pitch: An unexplained (yet theorized) scientific phenomena referred to as "Earthquake lights". Strange lights that seem to appear in the skies whilst (usually high-magnitude) earthquakes form. However, what isn't expected is that these are entities made of light, appearing to simply spectate the earthquakes. Why they do this is found out in the tale.

Central Narrative: During a high-magnitude earthquake near Site [REDACTED], there were "Earthquake Lights" spotted by many people. As this is a scientifically unexplained phenomena, MTF Unit Rho-10 "Shaken, Not Stirred" (an MTF unit created to withstand seismic activity, or unnatural geological movement) enters the scene to investigate. After recordings are taken, and the film is placed through numerous filters & analysations, it's found that each of these 'strobes' of light contain a nearly humanoid entity which seems to be watching the earthquakes. When another high-magnitude earthquake occurs near the same area within the next month, the same dispatch is sent to investigate these flashes of light closer. As the protagonist, codename "Charlie-0" (or C-0 by military alphabets) approaches towards the light, it seems to remain still for much longer than previous. They go to the top of the nearest destroyed building via an extremely long grappling hook and a lot of climbing. 23 minutes later, they arrive at the top, before the entity slowly floats down towards him. They take him somewhere - yet to be discovered. The man would slowly begin to communicate with these entities, finding out more and more about them - as the secrets reveal he continually updates the logs manually. Finally, when he's freed, he decides to watch one final earthquake with them. That's how it'd end, with a full log & a destroyed city.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that this could, hypothetically, be real is a big thing. Playing off of real world unexplained phenomena. Not to mention the fact it opens up as a tale-SCP has always caught my interest. A dangerous scenario (that being an earthquake) being traversed whilst also trying to gain intel on things which you can barely even see for more then a flash of a second is extremely difficult, and thrilling to read about.

Additional Notes: There is almost definitely some shit which I've messed up with the lore, as I am an idiot. Please feel free to be harsh in critique. Thank you!

item.title: Re: Transfer consciousness to a non-physical entity
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, Caspian2. Thank you, again, for reading my concept and giving me feedback.

From what I understand, you seem to approve SCP-XXXX's physical functions and the historical background. Your biggest concern, however, is understanding SCP-XXXX-1, imagining the object and its lack of tension. I will gladly discuss these elements.

+ More detailed explanation
- Hide

What exactly is SCP-xxxx-1? What exactly is this “non-physical entity right next to SCP-XXXX”?

I acknowledge your trouble with understanding SCP-XXXX-1, as the description was somewhat shallow. SCP-XXXX-1 is an invisible entity that contains the consciousness of the subject within SCP-XXXX. A ghost would be the most fitting description. I suppose what confuses you the most is why SCP-XXXX-1 is summoned right next to the capsule. No excuses here, it was just bad creativity. I only added that part because I thought it would confuse readers if I had not specified the location of SCP-XXXX-1's occurrence. I must rethink this occurrence.

But I’m having trouble actually picturing the object.

That can only mean there's trouble with my wording. To sum it up, imagine a metallic cylinder big enough to contain a human inside of it, hence it is the "sleeping capsule". The capsule has another metallic compound attached underneath it to ensure it doesn't roll sideways.
Here's an image for inspiration.
The image is obviously not the actual SCP, but to visualize the object's dimensions.

There isn’t much intrigue, tension or conflict present in the concept.

Agreed, it is pretty boring and opposes no threat whatsoever. Since this is my first concept, I wanted to start off small, since I read somewhere on this website that dangerous doesn't always make it interesting. Due to the limited quantity of words, I could not write the procedures. In fact, there is some danger/caution when using this capsule. As mentioned, the gas will continuously flow inside the capsule to ensure the subject stays asleep. Obviously, this would increase the concentration of the anesthesia-alike gas, and decrease the volume of oxygen over a period of time, making the subject suffocate in their sleep. Therefore, there must always be another personnel nearby to keep track of the oxygen saturation with a gadget such as pulse oximeter. But again, this is no threat towards mankind which is why, I presume, makes it so boring.

One way you can try fixing this is adding some element of danger to the scp. So it can transport people around, but use it too often / too long, and there will be detrimental effects, for example.

One danger element is as mentioned above, suffocation after a long period of time. The idea of being transported to random locations sounds interesting. The first idea to my concept was a gas mask that, once attached to the user, has same effect as the capsule, but was scratched once I learned about SCP-1499 which is basically a gas mask that transports the user to a random location. However, I approve the idea about harmful side effects which I will take into consideration.

Revision

I will revise or go in depth with the following elements:

  • Threat/danger - Suffocation, harsh side effects, unpredictable teleportations
  • SCP-XXXX-1 - Reconsider capabilities (hereby laws of physics and nature)
  • Writing - Simpler descriptions

Perhaps more points will be added later on, but this is what I assume I should focus on for now.

item.title: Re: Super Turbo Laser Motorcarriage
item.content:encoded:
1) You need to keep the old man around a little longer for the sake of the narrative, but cybersqyd touched on that pretty well so I'll basically leave it alone. I'll just mention that it would feel better if he ended up letting the car go on his own, including his loss, rather than relying on The Foundation's devices.

2) The big problem I have is that if the car becomes more destructive the faster it goes but then slows down the more damage it does. However, the car is able to evade capture despite any roadblocks placed in front of it; that doesn't work. if it does significant damage to the roadblock then it should also be slowed down significantly as well, or at least be a far easier target. If the reaction speed also slows down, then this means that the vehicle not only slows down after a collision but also will take longer to get back up to speed.

In short, while it would be able to get past a roadblock, it wouldn't get away from any pursuers, especially if they were ready for it once it got past the roadblock.

3) You may also want to debate the "reduces to atoms" part. Most items used for roadblocks contain a lot of hydrogen and oxygen as part of their make-up; if you reduce items to their atomic components, then that releases all that oxygen and hydrogen to the general area. The fun part here is that oxygen and hydrogen when given a chance combine rather violently into water when given the chance; the explosion is pretty powerful and pretty exothermic.

Now, remember how the vehicle slows down based on how much damage it does? This means that if it does enough damage to slow it down significantly, not only is it going to create a massive explosion, but it's also not going to have the speed necessary to escape the explosion.

You may want to consider stepping it back to a "molecular level" explosion so that it's basically destroyed, but with no nasty side effects.

Interesting idea, but it needs a few tweaks.

I initially didn't like this SCP - because it conflicts with my headcanon that all the anomalous stuff of the Foundation-verse is natural to the multiverse.

Like, every universe has something a little weird about it - the Foundation-verse is just a place where the barriers between realities have frayed, so there's been a bit of cross-pollination between realities and that's why the Foundation-verse has LOTS of different kinds of weird shit.

But… how can they be sure there are no anomalies and no Foundation equivalent?

The US government-B says they know nothing about anomalies or a Foundation equivalent. However… if Foundation-B was doing there jobs properly, the politicians wouldn't know, would they?

I love the idea that there are anomalies and a Foundation - it's just their Foundation is much more effective than ours. Every potentially dangerous SCP (including ones that are barely contained in baseline) was either neutralised or permanently contained, and the few anomalies that are still uncontained are pretty much harmless/unnoticeable.

Because they're more effective, they don't need to reach out for government co-operation and, aside from a few paranoid types in secret service agencies, nobody knows they even exist, let alone what their purpose is.

item.title: Re: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
My core concern with this as a SCP article is that whilst the central narrative section definitely feels emotional and hard hitting in the right way, it also feels like the actual story being told is eminently predictable as soon as the characters are introduced, especially considering the description of what the pom poms do is gonna be before the addenda containing the narrative. Indeed, even the description alone is enough to chart out the story: the actual progression just, does exactly what you would expect from a thing that sucks the happiness out a person and sends it to everyone around them.

My advice here would be to consider how you can make this land better. Perhaps it'd be by making this a tale told from the perspective of the webcam logs where the behaviour of the pom poms is deliberately being hidden from the reader; perhaps it's by subverting the narrative path somehow, whether by having someone intervene at the final moment or by like, really showing the effect too much happiness is having on the family too and having that be almost more of the focus or something else.

item.title: Re: The Dark Lantern
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Interviews with the creature (it is sapient and capable of speech) and history of its manifestations. It has been around for a long time.

So like, this is going to be the bulk of your narrative but like…what happens here? What story do the interviews tell? What does the history of it's manifestations add?

My concern is you don't really have a cohesive story around this so much as a weird DnD monster; and if you don't have the story down, this won't work.

The actual core anomaly feels…fine but a touch overcomplex perhaps: it has a lot of elements to it that feel a little like they don't necessarily add much; but without having a better idea of what you want to do with the article, I can't tell whether this overcomplexity matters. I guess at it's core my question is: why does this thing bother turning humans into wood in order to burn them in it's lantern instead of like, just using regular wood when it's in a forest? Like obviously narratively, that's more interesting; but the anomaly feels like it needs a motivation for this, y'know?

IMO: just have folk be tempted by a weird song they hear in the woods that makes them go 'wtf is that' and investigate; you don't need to like, making it so that they're forced to be affected by it (at least, that's what I'm assuming the cognitohazard does here)

item.title: Re: Image-Shifting Painting
item.content:encoded:
My concern is that this feels too close to Banksy's painting shredding except it's anomalous in a vague way that's not hugely interesting to me?

In part, this is because the images it shows are described as 'seemingly meaningless images', which is then followed up with 'foundation logo over the faces of multiple different paintings' and it kinda feels like there's this progression here where the painting is kinda, mocking the foundation but it's not really saying anything or doing anything interesting with this; and I'm left just…feeling like this would be a relatively bland test log where there's a lot of 'we got a d-class to look at the painting, it was a weird forest huh; we got a d-class to look at the painting, it was a random restaurant scene but everyone's face had the foundation logo on it' and it just…won't be interesting?

I think the core of this, the idea that the painting's depictions change based on who's observing it, is good; and I like the idea of AWCY? using this to troll the Foundation; but I think it actually needs to capture that: the images shown in the painting have to actually be meaningful in some manner, they have to make the Foundation do something, and then they have to get the 'lol it was all a prank bro' message, y'know?

item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit

My, central concern with this as a story is that you're setting up Dr Fox as the protagonist of the story but they aren't actually a particularly active part of the story, instead being dragged from event to event where she just kinda, reacts to what's happening in a pretty passive way instead of like, her actually being the driving force of the story.

Beyond this, it's just…not very interesting as a narrative? There's a murder monster, it does some murder, it disappears, there's a bit of investigation and then we learn why it does murders but there's not really any sense of there being like…stakes to this discovery or anything and it doesn't really reframe what's happening in an interesting way.

I guess really what this needs is character motivation: Fox needs a reason to be so invested in figuring out what's happening beyond just 'its her job!'; and the dark dog needs a reason to like…have this whole ritual happen and to attack the other dogs. I think the ritual also just kinda passively happening feels weird too? Like, nothing makes it happen and so it's just…kinda a thing that happens to happen. The angle of there being like, Damien and this dog working together to manifest the dark dog isn't awful but it needs to feel purposeful: like, if this was them manifesting a dark dog to like, get revenge on the people that wronged Damien or to hunt down his murderer or w/e, it'd land a lot better; but instead it's just…a weird ritual?

item.title: Admin Post
item.content:encoded:
We aren't responsible for them, but we have a responsibility to keep the site itself as out-of-fire as possible.

We have the capacity to exert some level of control over who is reading our work; that's this splash page, really. And since we *know* we have minors reading our wiki, we decided as staff to set these splash pages up to block off non-members from reading potentially objectionable material.

And 231 is potentially objectionable by the arbitrary standards set by the staff involved with the decision.

Please don't continue this conversation, and do not reply to this admin post. We are keeping the splash page up, I'm sorry that it bugs you but we won't be changing our decision for the foreseeable future.

item.title: Re: Super Turbo Laser Motorcarriage
item.content:encoded:
This feels, somewhat reminiscent of SCP-5141 but with a little less subtlety to it; and less of an old time-y focus.

The…character focussed nature of this feels… iffy? I don't necessarily dislike it; but my concern is that too much of the actually interesting events have happened before the interviews start, and that there's not enough narrative meat to the interviews to actually like, carry the whole article upon them? Like, my concern with the interviews is really that they have a character focus but there's not really a sense of like, the stuntman being forced to reckon with what he's done, and grow as a person and like…accept that he can't just self destruct or w/e. Like theoretically the growth of him getting released and making friends with car enthusiasts is a fine ending here, but he doesn't actually get to make this growth: the ethics committee amnesticises him and so it's basically forced to happen.

I think if you want to make this narratively work as a thing around the old man, you've gotta figure out how he changes during the course of this; like, even if it's just like, him reminiscing with the foundation about old jobs he did and him coming to realise he's had a good life and he doesn't need this big…glitzy ending, y'know? Or perhaps realising that there's still people he cares about who are alive or something?

My concern with the testing after it is that it doesn't really narratively build off what came before or anything; and it just feels tacked on at the end; and I'd probably cut this; the focus is on the man, and anything that doesn't serve that arc isn't really…necessary?

item.title: Re: Draft: Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for answers to your questions
– hide block

It sounds like I should be focusing less on the open-mystery aspect that lots of SCPs (especially earlier ones) tend to use, and focus more on disclosing a full story with only small amounts of vague subtleties, is that somewhat accurate? Admittedly I am taking inspiration more from Series 1 than the more recent series.

Open mystery is like…fine when you have a concept that supports this: like, SCP-4391 is a relatively recent example of something that's just, openly highly mysterious about what's going on. The problem here is that the mystery of this…just isn't necessarily very interesting? Which is why a more concrete narrative arc is a good idea (which doesn't mean 'don't be subtle', it just means, 'the subtlety has to actually add something')

I'm thinking one of the best ways to clarify the story in the addenda is to turn Addendum 3 into full interviews with the father and the doctor, which will also disclose more origin story material for the skip, and make it more relatable/sympathetic. Does this sound like something that would work? Would the Foundation do something like that, i.e. visit them in person under the guise of a separate government organization, instead of just making a phone call?

My, concern with this is that it feels like it would add a lot of backstory to this without really adding much that's interesting (i.e., that this feels too much like an info dump of material that doesn't necessarily add a tonne).

I can definitely shorten the description by at least 20-25%, maybe almost half. I get the impression that I should instead put almost all of my focus into the addenda. I think 3000 words total would be the high end I should go for, but would that seem disproportionate to put so much of the material into these sections? Most SCPs I see tend not to have more than 5 addenda, unless it's intended as a lengthy epic.

I don't think this is a huge concern tbh. Like, use as many addendum and as many words as you need to convey what you need to: the problem with the description is that it provides a lot of detail that covers how it works exactly that like, the first addendum directly shows in a more effective/interesting manner.

The "closure" I intend to make is that the creature's desire is to achieve closure with the father character by meeting him. This is something that I think the Foundation would never allow even if they understood that's what it wants, which is why I don't end with a solid conclusion, but rather with the indefinite freezing, to imply it never gets what it wants (though I intend to modify the specifics here). Do you disagree, and feel the creature should achieve this?

See, the indefinite freezing can grant closure, it just doesn't here. For it to work, it has to provoke an emotional reaction in the reader: we have to want the SCP to reach the father because we think e.g. it would achieve something, perhaps a sense of closure for the SCP, perhaps a partial/full reversal of the situation, perhaps allowing the SCP to get revenge say; and then for us to be invested in this happening; so that a final note saying e.g. 'due to budget concerns, further testing has been suspended indefinitely.' lands because we actually care.

In the current version, the indefinite freezing doesn't land because it's effectively the status quo already: it's not a new development.

item.title: Re: Corpse of a Dead God
item.content:encoded:
Great write-up, but this is just the beginning.

1) The basic problem is that there is no visible SCP involvement. Even if it is just cursory that needs to be allowed for somewhere, be it an inspection by a Foundation agent, temporary control, or some other option. It's even possible for someone close to the CEO to a double-agent and feeding information to The Foundation; given his interest in the occult, it's a good fit.

2) There's far too much mystery here. What happened to him and his followers is of interest, and it needs to be given a reason of some sort. It doesn't matter if they became animals themselves, become a copse, have just decided to create a mystery cult to defend the body from others, or even another force has started eliminated everyone for the body, but their fate needs to be drawn out or at least hinted at.

Again, overall this is great write-up. There are some minor grammatical errors, but otherwise it's a good start!

item.title: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: I just listened to TheVolgun’s fantastic audio rendition of SCP-2137 and was very fascinated with the article as a whole.

The article mentions that highly secret details of the Foundation were leaked on YouTube and iTunes and the efforts to cover up the iTunes incident were imperfect.

It stands to reason then, that maybe some sheltered person hiding behind a sophisticated proxy, or something, managed to download and listen to the songs without having his memory erased, or even being noticed by the Foundation.

I feel that a story following this character as he becomes obsessed trying to get to the bottom of the SCP foundation would be an interesting read.

Central Narrative: I believe the protagonist of this tale would perhaps be some kind of techno-master who spends hours delving into the internet for obscure media. Someone who would notice a strange new album from Tupac appearing on Beyoncé’s iTunes page before it got taken down. The type of guy whose basement is filled with GPUs mining Bitcoin.

I think it would also make sense for this character to be as “off grid” as possible while still having internet access. So he hears about these songs, that sound a lot like Tupac, that are supposedly revealing deeply hidden truths about the world and he pounces on it. Buys the album without a second thought, backs up the songs on multiple drives, and devotes endless effort to figuring out what they mean.

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

Perhaps the story could also alternate between perspectives as foundation agents realize there’s a civilian who’s onto them.

I think ultimately the tale would end with the protagonist learning much more than any typical civilian would ever hope to. Like witnessing one or more SCPs firsthand, but getting killed in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most tales I’ve read are from the perspective of either Foundation Agents, someone in a GoI, or an SCP. I don’t know of many from the perspective of civilians. I also think the leaks from SCP-2137 are an event ripe for exploration.

Additional Notes: I’m returning to the SCP wiki after a fairly long absence so I’m sure there are things I’ve missed. I originally formatted this post wrong because last time I posted here no such thing existed. So if this idea has been done, or if it’s very similar to another tale, please let me know!

item.title: Lonely voice
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fantasy, and Supernatural

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a voice that talks to you when you're alone, separate from any other human contact for a time. It starts as your own thoughts, and diverges from your normal train of thought without your notice. Some people are more inclined to hear it, even when around others, but it talks to anyone separate from humanity for an extended period of time.

Central Narrative: It starts with a psych patient being evaluated for possible anomaly, but a suggestion by one of scientist puts forward the idea that an SCP may be attracted to the situation the patient was in—he had lived alone for many years, secluded. Tests are done putting people in isolation, and many attest to a divergence of thought from their normal thoughts after a time. This is chalked up to normal psychological phenomena, until patterns are seen in the thought patterns: many suggest being drawn away to be separate from humanity, such as going to isolated geographical places, as well as questioning social norms. Several of the test subjects are found to be heading to isolated areas in forests, and atop buildings over following weeks. Basically, the scientists come to the conclusion that the source of the thoughts are voices coming from a variety of non physical beings that dwell in places less inhabited by humans.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that it's relatable.

Additional Notes: Ehm, as a possible addition to the narrative, these beings are speculated to be aiding it trying to separate humans from each other one by one, as to aid in making an easier invasion of their own species.
